title: DR1 tells the trader what a consignment contact address is; the frontend only tells them what happens when they pick one.

controls.text: Selecting a contact copies their name and address into this notification.

finding.frontend: The only guidance on the page is the radios' hint, "Selecting a contact copies their name and address into this notification." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/copy/copy.en.js:4, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/contact/template.njk:20). It describes what the control does, which the trader can see for themselves, and says nothing about who the contact should be or what they are being signed up for. fe-contact then lists thirteen organisations with no basis on which to choose between them.
finding.prototype: DR1 opens the page with a definition of the role: "This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks." (app/views/contact-address-for-consignment.html:50-52). The list beneath it is headed "Select an address" (:62), so the definition sits between the h1 and the choice, where a trader reads it before deciding.
finding.difference: Replace the mechanism sentence with DR1's definition, as an intro paragraph between the heading and the radios rather than as a hint on the fieldset. The sentence carries a real obligation — it tells the trader the contact must be reachable through border checks — which is the thing the frontend currently leaves them to guess.
finding.falsifiedBy: The definition sentence, or any sentence describing who the contact should be, appearing in the frontend contact copy.

relatedTo.why: the definition is what makes the narrowed list make sense to a trader
